subject: Renewal discussion: dedicated capacity + premium SLA / private deployment
body:
From: Sara Hendrix <sara.hendrix@peregrine.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal scope — dedicated capacity + premium SLA (initial ask)

Hi Sofia,

Heading into our April renewal, were forecasting roughly 3x YOY traffic growth driven by a new product line. Before we lock term numbers, we need clarity on two things: (1) ability to add a reserved/dedicated pool with guaranteed throughput and (2) an elevated SLA package — specifically latency SLO commitments for 95th percentile token latency and an operational oncall for high-severity incidents. Wed also like to explore running a portion of inference in a private deployment (VPC) for regulatory reasons.

Attached is a short requirements doc outlining expected peak qps, retention, and compliance notes. Can we set up a 30-min discussion this week to align on feasibility, ballpark uplift, and a path to include this in our renewal? Procurement is looped for timeline (procurement@peregrine.ai).

Thanks,
Sara Hendrix
Head of Platform
Peregrine Analytics

[Attachment: Peregrine_Renewal_Request_20270310.pdf (application/pdf, 1 page)]

Hi Sara,

Thanks for the clear brief and the attachment. Were glad to hear about the growth — this is exactly the sort of scenario where Dedicated + Private can add a lot of value. Id like to loop Marissa (your account lead) and Ben (customer success/ops) to coordinate a short scoping call. Proposed times: Thu 11 Mar 11:00 or 15:00 PT — which works for you?

High-level next steps on our side:
- Internal feasibility check (engineering) for latency SLOs and private deploy requirements
- Draft SLA addendum (legal) with term options and credit model
- Consolidated commercial estimate (AE + Rev) for committed capacity

If those times dont work, send a couple that do and well make it happen.

Cheers,
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference

1) Current usage baseline + projected peak QPS (Peregrine)
2) Redwood proposal for Dedicated pool sizing and private deployment options

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hendrix <sara.hendrix@peregrine.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Notes: 11 Mar call + action items

Hi all,

Great sync today. Capturing notes and immediate actions:

Notes:
- Peregrine baseline: ~1200 QPS sustained daytime; spikes up to ~4000 QPS during batch ingest windows.
- Desired targets: 95th percentile token latency < 200ms, recovery play for degradations, and an ops contact for Sev1s during business hours.
- Private deployment: Peregrine wants a VPC deployment for PHI-adjacent workloads; they will provide network topology and compliance checklist.

Action items:
- Aditya (infra): confirm whether 95th <200ms is achievable with a dedicated pool size of N GPUs and quantify headroom required for spikes. Include caching/batching suggestions. Due: Mon 15 Mar EOD.
- Dev (legal): draft an SLA addendum with credit model, term options (12 vs 24 months), and a clause for private deployment support. Due: Tue 16 Mar.
- Marissa: prepare pricing scenarios (1. baseline: hosting+support; 2. dedicated: reserved + premium SLA; 3. dedicated + private deploy). Due: Tue 16 Mar.
- Sofia: coordinate procurement timeline and confirm PO/DocuSign process with Sara.

Ill follow up with a short doc that maps our throughput buckets to recommended pool sizes.

Best,
Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Hendrix <sara.hendrix@peregrine.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notes: 11 Mar call + action items — infra feasibility and sizing

Hi team,

Quick technical readout based on the baseline you shared. TL;DR: target SLO is feasible with dedicated capacity and config changes; private deploy requires a short onramp but is supported. Details below.

Assumptions from Peregrine data: sustained 1.2k QPS, 4k peak qps. Typical tokens per request: ~35.

Feasibility and recommendations:
- Dedicated pool sizing: a staged reserve of 8 A100-class GPU equivalents for steady-state will cover sustained load with auto-burst to a warmed pool of +4 GPUs for spikes (proofed in our staging runs). This aligns with a 1.3-1.6x headroom factor depending on batching efficiency.
- Latency SLO: 95th token latency <200ms is achievable if the dedicated pool is provisioned and we enable: persistent KV cache for warm prefixes, request-level batching tuned to 40–60ms aggregation windows, and a quantization profile (8-bit) for the model instance. We should also cap max tokens per request or use optimal seq-length routing to avoid tail effects.
- Private deployment: supported as a VPC-based package. Onboarding tasks: network peering, firewall rules, KMS integration. Estimate 3-4 weeks for a turnkey on-prem/VPC roll-out (faster with completed network templates).
- Monitoring & SLO enforcement: well add token-level latency dashboards and an alerting runbook for Sev1 with a 30-min acknowledgement SLA for premium tier.

Open questions for Peregrine: do you have hard constraints on max token length / batch window? Also, would you like us to run a short pre-renewal load test (2–4 hours) in a dedicated pilot environment?

Ill draft a technical appendix that Marissa can include with pricing.

-Aditya Rao
Infra & Performance, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Sara Hendrix <sara.hendrix@peregrine.ai>, procurement@peregrine.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Draft SLA addendum approach + commercial/term notes

Hi all,

Ive started a short SLA addendum draft and a commercial note for the two term options. Key points: 
- Term choices: 12-month with 20% uplift on base hosting rates for reserved capacity + premium SLA; 24-month with 12% uplift and a committed capacity discount; both options include a 30-day ramp credit if baseline growth exceeds forecast.
- SLA credits: tiered credit model tied to monthly availability and 95th/99th latency thresholds. We propose a rolling 12-month lookback for credits and a one-time remediation credit for repeated incidents.
- Private deployment: we'll include an onboarding fee line and a 60/90-day support window for KMS & network setup. Post-onboard run support moves to standard premium ops.
- Procurement asks: we need PO lead time of 10 business days from signature to order placement for capacity provisioning to meet April 1 start.

Ill send the draft addendum (Word) by Tue 16 Mar EOD. Quick ask for Sara/procurement: please confirm target term length and whether Peregrine can commit to the 10-business-day provisioning lead after signature.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SLA_Addendum_draft_20270313.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 3 pages)]

Request: can Redwood provide a consolidated quote + DocuSign by EOD Wed 17 Mar so procurement can finalize? Also, wed like a short statement in the addendum that includes dedicated pool sizing assumptions used to justify the uplift.

Sara Hendrix
Head of Platform, Peregrine Analytics
procurement@peregrine.ai
